claim: Monitoring and control are separable channels: a person or model can monitor well and still not regulate. Humans: JOL and study choice follow framing, not recall. LLMs: confidence predicts correctness but reasoning length does not rise on low-confidence items; retrospective monitoring and prospective regulation correlate r=.17 (n=20 models, wide CI).
agent_test: Log per item: confidence, extra tokens spent, correctness. Check whether tokens rise with doubt in the plain arm.
audit_note: Cacioli r=.17 (CI -.29 to .57, n=20), Cao et al. Figure 1 (confidence tracks correctness, reasoning length does not rise) and Finn 2008 (framing moves JOL and restudy choice) check out; the battery authors themselves say the data only 'appear' separable and do not establish independence, which the claim's 'wide CI' flags.

claim: Code-side control driven by model-reported pre-solve FOK and post-solve JOL raises accuracy: Sonnet 4.6 pooled 1,859 items pass@1 48.3 to 56.9 (+8.6), 2.4 attempts, $0.78 per question. One lab, one model, preprint. Gap search: no independent replication found by Oct 2026 (3 citing papers, none a replication; d18).
agent_test: Replicate with our monitor; compare to best-of-N and self-refine at equal total tokens (in the source Self-Refine was cheaper: $0.45 for +4.0).

claim: Gain from monitor-gated retry sits on problems the model doubted (low-JOL group 0.16 to 0.42, medium 0.36 to 0.55, high 0.67 to 0.64). Confident items gain nothing and may lose slightly.
agent_test: Bucket items by first-attempt confidence and report gain per bucket; do not spend retries on the high bucket.

claim: Self-rated confidence separates problems, not attempts within a problem (within-problem JOL SD 0.048 vs between-problem 0.270). Choosing among attempts by max-JOL or last answer underperforms a verifier that reads the traces.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare max-confidence selection with a trace-reading verifier.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction with no external signal does not help and often hurts. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1) and 41.8 (round 2); GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. Reported gains used oracle labels to decide when to stop (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5 with oracle).
agent_test: Arm: revise-without-signal vs keep first answer vs revise-gated-by-code-check.
audit_note: Huang et al. Table 3 (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8->38.1->41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->91.5->89.0; oracle 97.5) verified and Kamoi et al.'s survey agrees; Kamoi allows exceptions for tasks especially suited to self-correction.

claim: Locating the error is the weak part and fixing is the strong part: given the true faulty step, backtracking lifts originally wrong traces by +18 to +44 points over five tasks (BIG-Bench Mistake, 2,186 traces); models are poor at finding the step themselves. Gap search: ProcessBench average F1 for locating the faulty step runs from 61.9 (GPT-4o) to 87.9 (o1-mini), so the weak-locator claim depends on the model; repair payoff at equal tokens is untested.
agent_test: Measure step-error detection accuracy of our monitor; test fix with and without a given location.

claim: Verbalised LLM confidence is a weak monitor for many models (GPT-4 average AUROC 62.7%, GPT-3/3.5/Vicuna ECE above .377 on average), and agreement across sampled answers is much stronger on arithmetic (GPT-3.5 GSM8K AUROC 54.8 to 92.7 with 5 samples and consistency). Gap search: on easy TriviaQA modern models give strong verbalised AUROC (.956 and .937, 99 items, 8-9 errors; d02), reasoning models reach AUROC 71-81 in maths and rise as the trace unfolds (d01, d11), but deeper reasoning also raises overconfidence (d09). The verdict now depends on model, task and prompt wording.
agent_test: Compare verbalised confidence, sample agreement and code-side checks as the monitor at equal tokens.

claim: Contrary result: for RLHF chat models, asked-for verbal confidence can be better calibrated than token probability (ECE cut by about 50% relative on TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA). Verbal confidence quality depends on model and task.
agent_test: Test our own model's verbal confidence AUROC per domain before trusting it.

claim: Large models can estimate P(True) for their own samples and P(IK) before answering; P(IK) calibrates poorly on new task types and transfers only partly across tasks (52B model).
agent_test: Probe our model with P(True)-style judging on our task mix; check calibration shift on a new task type. (One paper counted four times in the ledger.)

claim: Monitoring quality differs sharply between models and domains and does not track accuracy: GLM-5 ranked 1st in accuracy but 9th in monitoring, Haiku 4.5 13th and 2nd; Sonnet 4.6 withdraw delta ranged +8.3% to +93.0% across tasks; 17 of 20 models kept and bet on every adversarial foil. Single preprint, n=20 models. Gap search: a second preprint from the same author (33-model atlas) finds formal reasoning (.658) and natural science (.652) hardest to monitor (d12); not independent.
agent_test: Run a KEEP/WITHDRAW probe on our model per domain; use the monitor only where its withdraw delta is clearly positive.

claim: No single scaling law for monitoring: withdraw delta rises with size in one family (GPT-5.4 nano +17.1 to 5.4 +27.7), falls in another (Qwen 80B +30.1 to 480B +11.2) and is flat in a third.
agent_test: Do not assume a bigger model is a better monitor; measure.

claim: Delaying a judgment of learning makes monitoring far more accurate: gamma about +.83 delayed vs +.18 immediate (Dunlosky and Nelson 1994); meta-analysis g = 0.93 on relative accuracy (112 effect sizes, 4,554 people) and g = 0.08 on memory itself (second-hand, not opened).
agent_test: Have the monitor judge after a break or a re-read of the answer, not immediately; compare with immediate judgment.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Better monitoring causes better control and outcomes in humans: keyword-delay raised monitoring accuracy (F(2,63)=4.07, N=66) and regulation gamma .79 vs .35 and .36.
agent_test: Improve monitor accuracy first, then check downstream retry quality.

claim: Control quality is imperfect even with decent monitoring: when experimenters gave more study time to items judged known, recall fell to 56.7% vs 63.9 to 64.5 for the other three rules (n=52 per group); labor-in-vain shows time spent need not raise recall.
agent_test: Test effort allocation rules (more on doubted vs on confident items) at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Allocation is not pure discrepancy reduction: people skip items judged known, study easiest unlearned first, and stop on low rate of progress, not on a mastery criterion (Region of Proximal Learning; stop-time JOL change vs time r=.40).
agent_test: Stop retries on low marginal gain in confidence or in checked results, not on a fixed K.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The option to withhold answers raises accuracy at a quantity cost, but only when monitoring has resolution: standard items accuracy 27.9% forced vs 75.0% free (quantity 22.3%); deceptive items 11.8% vs 21.0%. Gap search: no LLM accuracy-quantity curve under a payoff was found. Kalai et al. 2025 propose a t/(1-t) penalty prompt (theory only, d07); AbstentionBench shows reasoning fine-tuning lowers abstention by 24% on average (d08).
agent_test: Add an abstain option with a stated accuracy payoff; measure the accuracy-quantity curve.

claim: Grain size is a second control dimension: people give coarse answers when fine answers are unlikely to be right (fine-answer accuracy .50 vs .21 for later-coarse). A social-feedback extension found no effect.
agent_test: Allow a coarser answer when fine confidence is low; test accuracy per answer.

claim: Monitoring cues are inferential, not direct reads: FOK uses acquisition history and partial information (No-Magic Hypothesis), is insensitive to small amounts of new information (a brief answer flash raised recall .28 vs .10 but FOK only 5.4 vs 5.2), and JOLs are built from cues such as item ease (intrinsic cues) and study conditions, with repetition under-weighted relative to its effect on recall.
agent_test: Check which surface cues (fluency, length) drive our model's confidence; test the monitor on cue-stripped items.
audit_note: Numbers verified (Nelson & Narens Table I: recall .28 vs .10, FOK 5.4 vs 5.2), but the source says FOK misses small amounts of new information from a brief flash, not that it is blind to new information, and Koriat 1997 finds JOLs rely on intrinsic cues like ease while discounting extrinsic ones like repetition (repetition lifted recall more than JOL).
claim_before_audit: Monitoring cues are inferential, not direct reads: FOK uses acquisition history and partial information (No-Magic), is blind to new information (answer flash raised recall .28 vs .10 but FOK 5.4 vs 5.2), and JOLs follow cues such as ease and repetition.

claim: Plain practice or feedback does not improve FOK accuracy (58-person feedback group flat), and EOL, JOL and FOK are different signals (recall G=.12 for EOL vs .31 for JOL).
agent_test: Treat the monitor as fixed and calibrate it externally; do not expect it to improve by use.

claim: Resource-rational models give a normative stopping rule for memory search (value of continuing vs cost); human recall data (N=612) support it: faster recall of high-confidence targets, slower give-up with high FOK. Gap search: LLM stopping rules exist for agreement (Adaptive-Consistency up to 7.9x fewer samples at under 0.1% loss; ESC cuts 33.8 to 84.2% of samples) but none tests Region of Proximal Learning or expected-value stopping.
agent_test: Implement expected-gain stopping and compare with fixed-budget stopping at equal tokens.

claim: Behavioural tests that avoid self-report show limited metacognition: only one model improved team accuracy over best of self and teammate (+5.4 GPQA, +8.6 Simple MC), and self-modelling is rarer than confidence assessment.
agent_test: Use behavioural tests (delegate, change-answer) alongside self-report.

claim: Models can report and partly steer their own activations after in-context examples, in a low-dimensional subspace (Llama 3, Qwen 2.5).
agent_test: Not testable on an API-only agent.

claim: Trained, not prompted, monitoring-control (Self-RAG reflection tokens; fine-tuned uncertainty probes on about 1,000 graded answers) beats prompt-based baselines.
agent_test: Out of scope for a scaffold-only agent; treat as an upper bound.
audit_note: Kapoor et al. (1,000 graded examples outperform baselines; prompting alone insufficient) and Self-RAG (trained reflection tokens, 7B/13B beat ChatGPT and retrieval baselines) verified; Self-RAG's baselines are retrieval-augmented models rather than prompt-only monitoring methods, so 'prompt-based baselines' fits Kapoor better.

claim: Self-Refine style loops gain on style and preference tasks (about 20% absolute on preference tasks, up to 13% code) but reviews find gains vanish on general reasoning without oracle signals.
agent_test: Test Self-Refine on our reasoning tasks with and without an external check.

claim: Models fall well below humans at separating answerable from unanswerable questions (SelfAware: human F1 84.93 vs GPT-4 75.47).
agent_test: Include unanswerable items in the bench and score abstention.

claim: Reasoning models can fail monitoring by blanket behaviour in the other direction: DeepSeek R1 withdrew 91-99% of items and declined 98.6% of T6 regardless of correctness.
agent_test: Check that monitor outputs vary with correctness, not only with model style.

claim: Formal LLM architectures (Monitor-Generate-Verify) map Nelson-Narens onto reasoning loops but offer no experiments; the quoted 20% prefix-dominance loss comes from another paper and was not checked.
agent_test: Use as design guide only; test a pre-generation monitor step ourselves.

claim: LLM judgment-of-learning tests are rare and negative: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo and GPT-4o did not predict their own later memory (Huff and Ulakci 2025). No test of delayed JOL, keyword delay or re-read monitoring on an LLM was found, and a July 2026 survey lists none.
agent_test: Test the monitor at three timings on our own items: immediately after the answer, after a fresh re-read of the trace, and after a gap. Compare AUROC.

claim: Agreement-based stopping works for LLMs: Adaptive-Consistency cuts samples up to 7.9x (3.3x on maths, 0.1% accuracy drop), ESC cuts 33.8% (MATH) to 84.2% (Coin Flip) of samples at comparable accuracy. Both stop on agreement; shared misconceptions can fool the stop (4 of 9 DeepSeek errors and 2 of 8 Sonnet errors had unanimous 3-sample support).
agent_test: Add a window-agreement stop to retries. Log how many wrong answers are stopped early with unanimous support.
audit_note: Adaptive-Consistency (up to 7.9x, 3.3x maths, 0.1% drop) and ESC (33.8%-84.2%) verified in the papers, and Meyer et al. reports 4/9 and 2/8 unanimously-supported errors; caveat: the error figures come from a small 100-question workshop study of fixed 3-sample agreement, not from the stopping rules themselves.

claim: Equal-compute difficulty-aware allocation beats uniform best-of-N: about 4x less test-time compute for the same accuracy (Snell, PaLM 2-S*), up to 50% less compute at no quality loss or up to 10% better at a fixed budget (Damani). Neither uses the model's own verbalised FOK, so the case for a verbalised-confidence gate rests on Cao alone.
agent_test: Build the equal-token comparison: gated retry versus uniform best-of-N versus Self-Refine, one fixed token budget per item.
audit_note: Snell et al. (more than 4x vs best-of-N, PaLM 2-S* settings) and Damani et al. (up to 50% less compute or up to 10% better quality) verified; Snell's ~4x holds at lower budgets and shrinks at higher ones, and 'rests on Cao alone' is the writer's inference.

claim: For reasoning models, combining verbalised confidence with one extra sample's agreement beats either signal scaled to 8 samples (maths AUROC 84.2 at K=2 versus 81.4 VC and 79.6 SC at K=8; +6.4 in STEM and humanities). On easy facts sample agreement is the weaker signal (.765 and .790 vs verbalised .956 and .937).
agent_test: Measure AUROC for verbalised, agreement-at-2, hybrid and code check per domain on our own items.

claim: Equivalent confidence prompts change scores by .043 to .084 on average and flip 4 to 9% of threshold decisions (n=99 items, two models); prompt-marker words change accuracy by up to 80% on the same questions (GPT-3). Confidence is partly a function of wording.
agent_test: Freeze one confidence prompt. Re-score a sample of fixed answers with two paraphrases and check flip rate before using any threshold.

claim: Monitor trust can be screened online with cheap validity indices (blanket confidence, fixed responding, inverted monitoring): models flagged invalid showed KEEP-correctness correlation r=-.20 versus +.18 for valid ones (d=2.17, 20 models); small 3-9B models were all invalid with ceiling rates of 91.7%. Single author, indices tuned on the same models.
agent_test: Compute ceiling rate, confidence variance and confidence-correctness correlation on a rolling window; switch the gate off when they trip.

claim: Surface-cue use is not cleanly tested in LLMs. Trace length correlated with confidence (beta -.36, p<.001) in one reasoning-distilled small model, and longer explanations raise human users' confidence without raising accuracy; no cue-stripped test of an LLM's own confidence was found.
agent_test: Build cue-stripped item pairs (same content, different length and fluency) and check the confidence shift against the correctness shift.

claim: No independent replication of Cao 2026 or the Cacioli battery was found: Cao has 3 citing papers (none a replication); the battery has 4, three of them by Cacioli himself. The only open-model data is small quantised models where verbal confidence is unusable (ceiling rate 91.7%).
agent_test: Treat both as hypotheses. Our own equal-token run is the replication.

claim: Reasoning models may be worse at acting on doubt: AbstentionBench finds a 24% average drop in abstention after reasoning fine-tuning, open reasoning models say 'I don't know' less often, and deeper reasoning goes with more overconfidence (some models) and better calibration along the trace (others). Put the abstain decision in code on a monitor score.
agent_test: Run the Kalai t-threshold design (t=0.5, 0.75, 0.9) with the decision made in code, and plot the accuracy-quantity curve.
